name: GüvenTek Bilişim A.Ş.
summary: A 370-person technology company with an Istanbul HQ (ERP, mail, database), an Ankara operations branch and an Izmir R&D office holding all source code. Each office has its own /16 and FortiGate; offices are joined by IPsec VPN, default-deny everywhere, a guest VLAN that only reaches the internet, and FortiAnalyzer logs in Istanbul.

vlans.name: guest
vlans.note: Same guest range at every office; internet only.

chosen.reason: Sized for 350 Mbps of calculated need on a 500 Mbps fiber line, HA because the ERP and mail servers live here.

alternatives.reason: Strong app control for a mid-size HQ. (Reviewer-added comparison; not in the student's original submission.)
Fits Cisco switching. (Reviewer-added comparison; not in the student's original submission.)
Cost-effective small/mid gateway. (Reviewer-added comparison; not in the student's original submission.)
Easy management. (Reviewer-added comparison; not in the student's original submission.)

rules.note: ERP, mail and database servers sit in their own VLAN and are exposed only to staff.
Guest VLAN 99 reaches no internal server, internet only.
Torrent, P2P and illegal sites are blocked by Web Filter and Application Control.
Site-to-site IPsec VPN to Ankara and Izmir.
Default Deny: everything not explicitly allowed is dropped and logged.

rules.note: Nobody, including HQ management, reaches the R&D VLAN from outside; source code is the crown jewel.
Outbound data from R&D is under strict DLP rules to stop code leakage.
Default Deny: everything not explicitly allowed is dropped and logged.

remoteAccess.note: All offices reach the internet locally and are connected to each other by IPsec VPN.

monitoring.siem: All FortiGate logs go to a FortiAnalyzer (SIEM) server in the Istanbul HQ; Grafana-style NOC/SOC screens.
monitoring.owner: The IT and Security team in Istanbul during 09:00-18:00; an on-call IT staff member gets SMS for critical out-of-hours alerts.
monitoring.alertSink: Automatic e-mail (CPU over 80%, VPN down, critical IPS rule) and SMS to the on-call engineer.
monitoring.appVsSecurity: Not separated in the original; NOC screens show traffic while IPS/antivirus events come from FortiAnalyzer.
